ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $DA\perp AB$, $DA=6\,\text{cm}$, $\angle B+\angle C=150^\circ$, point $A$ is exactly the midpoint of $EB$, and $P$, $Q$ are moving points on the line segments $CE$, $BE$ respectively. What is the minimum value of $BP+PQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct point $F$ as the symmetric point of $B$ with respect to $CE$. Draw $BF$ and $EF$. Then, $EB=EF$,

since $\angle B + \angle C = 150^\circ$, it follows that $\angle BEC = 180^\circ - (\angle B + \angle C) = 30^\circ$. Since point $B$ is symmetric to point $F$ with respect to $EC$, it follows that $\angle BEC = \angle FEC = 30^\circ$, hence $\angle BEF = 60^\circ$, therefore $\triangle BEF$ is an equilateral triangle. Draw $BP$, $PF$, $PQ$, then $BP=FP$, therefore $BP + QP = FP + PQ$. Thus, when $F$, $P$, and $Q$ are on the same line and $FQ \perp EB$, then the minimum value of $BP+PQ$ is the length of $FQ$. At this moment, $Q$ coincides with the midpoint of $EB$, hence coincides with point $A$. Since $DA \perp AB$ and $DA=6$cm, it follows that $AE= 6\sqrt{3}$cm. In $\triangle QEF$, $FQ = \sqrt{3}AE = \sqrt{3} \times 6\sqrt{3} = \boxed{18}$cm. Therefore, the minimum value of $BP+PQ$ is $18$cm.
